related_questions.question: What will disqualify you from donating blood?

text_blocks.snippet: Several factors can disqualify a person from donating blood. These include certain medical conditions, high-risk behaviors, and recent medications or procedures. Some permanent disqualifications include a history of HIV or AIDS, hepatitis B or C, and certain cancers. Temporary deferrals may be in place for conditions like recent infections, some medications, and specific types of sexual activity.
snippet_highlighted_words: certain medical conditions, high-risk behaviors, and recent medications or procedures

list.title: HIV/AIDS:
list.snippet: A positive test for HIV or a diagnosis of AIDS permanently disqualifies an individual from donating blood.

list.title: Hepatitis B or C:
list.snippet: A history of hepatitis B or C infections, particularly those confirmed by laboratory testing, is a permanent exclusion.

list.title: Certain Cancers:
list.snippet: Individuals with leukemia or lymphoma, or those who have had a tissue or organ transplant involving living animal tissue or dura matter (brain covering), are generally permanently disqualified.

list.title: Certain Blood Disorders:
list.snippet: Conditions like sickle cell disease can be a permanent disqualification, though some individuals may be able to donate plasma.

text_blocks.snippet: Temporary Deferrals (Reasons to wait before donating):

list.title: Infections:
list.snippet: A fever or acute infection, a cold, the flu, or even a sore throat can lead to a temporary deferral.

list.title: Medications:
list.snippet: Certain medications, such as some blood thinners or medications used to prevent HIV, can result in a deferral period.

list.title: Recent Procedures:
list.snippet: A blood transfusion in the past 3 months, or certain surgical procedures may require a waiting period before donating.

list.title: High-Risk Behaviors:
list.snippet: Individuals who have engaged in risky sexual behaviors (like having sex for money or drugs, or having sex with someone who has HIV), or who have used needles to inject drugs, steroids, or anything not prescribed by a doctor may be deferred.

list.title: Travel:
list.snippet: Recent travel to certain countries or areas with endemic diseases may require a waiting period before donating.

list.title: Pregnancy:
list.snippet: Women who are pregnant are temporarily deferred from donating.

list.title: High or Low Blood Pressure:
list.snippet: Extremely high or low blood pressure readings can be a temporary disqualification.

list.title: Tattoos and Piercings:
list.snippet: Tattoos and piercings may require a waiting period before donating depending on the location and regulations of the donation center.
It's always best to check with the specific blood donation center or the American Red Cross for their specific eligibility requirements, as these can vary.
If you have any concerns about your eligibility, it's always a good idea to contact the donation center directly to discuss your specific situation.
